answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, reciprocal trades that counterparties later confirm; a fresh identity starts with no credit and must lock scarce tokens in escrow before receiving valuable goods. Splitting into many identities does not multiply trust, because each still needs independent partners and locked capital. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up more tokens and sustain more costly exchanges to build credible histories, while honest agents can treat the network like an island with a shared ledger, not a crystal knoll of instant, interchangeable accounts.
